Header: 2026-03-21 10:00 PDT  Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maria Chen (Redwood AE), Jonas Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Sapphire Lead Eng), Tom Keller (Platform Head), Priya Singh (Security)

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maria): hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maria from Redwood, i'll hand it to jonas for the SDK walkthrough in a sec
00:12 Speaker 2 (Jonas): hey all, morning  quick agenda: python + ts quickstarts, auth, env setup, console demo, then optimize tips and q&a
00:28 Speaker 3 (Aisha): thanks, we got about 40 minutes so good to focus on the integration steps, also priya will jump in on security questions
00:42 Speaker 2 (Jonas): great, so first the python SDK  the pip package is redwood-inference, basic flow is set env var REDWOOD_API_KEY, or for oauth you can use client creds and set REDWOOD_OAUTH_TOKEN, here's a snippet
01:10 Speaker 2 (Jonas): code: from redwood import Client; c = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) ; resp = c.generate('...')  that kind of thing, simple
01:33 Speaker 3 (Priya): quick q: is the api key stored in console, and how rotate keys?
01:40 Speaker 1 (Maria): yes keys are issued in console, you can create scoped tokens, rotate via the console or api, we also support KMS-wrapped keys for private deployments
01:58 Speaker 3 (Priya): ok good, need to document rotation policy for our audit team
02:10 Speaker 2 (Jonas): switching to typescript  npm package @redwood/inference, same pattern: const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }) ; streaming is supported via event listeners
02:35 Speaker 4 (Tom): are there typed examples for node lambda environment? we run node 18 in lambdas
02:42 Speaker 2 (Jonas): yes we have lambda quickstart in the repo, we'll share link  it includes batching examples too
03:05 Speaker 2 (Jonas): small note: in long-running server contexts use the persistent client and reuse the kv cache handle for prefix caching to lower token costs
03:30 Speaker 3 (Aisha): when you say kv cache handle, do you mean the prefix kv you guys mentioned in the docs? we have an internal redis instance
03:40 Speaker 2 (Jonas): exactly, Redwood's prefix caching can use redis or memcached, you can configure the cache backend in the SDK via REDWOOD_CACHE_URL, docs show examples
04:02 Speaker 3 (Aisha): perfect that's our plan, we prefer redis and will integrate that
04:20 Speaker 2 (Jonas): auth options  for enterprise we recommend private deployments with SSO + SAML, but for pilot you can use hosted with VPC peering and customer-managed keys (KMS), also support HSM certs for on-prem
04:48 Speaker 3 (Priya): on KMS: do you support AWS KMS and GCP KMS or just transfers?
04:54 Speaker 1 (Maria): we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations for Private; for Hosted we can integrate a customer-managed KMS for key wrapping
05:10 Speaker 4 (Tom): latency question  our SLAs are 200ms for the screening path, can you hit that on hosted?
05:18 Speaker 2 (Jonas): depends on model and seq length; for small models and short seqs hosted can be 50-120ms p50, but you should pin a model and do dedicated for consistent p95; we can run a benchmark
05:42 Speaker 3 (Aisha): what about batching impact? we need low latency but cost matters
05:48 Speaker 2 (Jonas): Optimize offers batching profiles: adaptive micro-batching that keeps latency SLO and groups requests to save tokens; we can tune batch size and max wait to trade cost/latency
06:12 Speaker 2 (Jonas): also mention quantization options  some models can be int8/4 and you'll lose a bit of quality but drop cost significantly, we'll recommend per-workload profiles
06:35 Speaker 3 (Priya): any misreports in logs or data residency concerns? our compliance team needs audit logs and retention controls
06:44 Speaker 1 (Maria): console exposes audit logs, per-route traces, and you can export audit logs to your SIEM  retention and export are configurable for Private deployments
07:05 Speaker 3 (Priya): great, please send SOC2 and architecture whitepaper
07:10 Speaker 1 (Maria): will do, adding to next steps
07:20 Speaker 2 (Jonas): hopping back to code, quick demo  i'll share my screen, opening the quickstart repo (note: audio may cut)
07:35 Speaker 2 (Jonas): python quickstart shows env example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY='sk_live_..' ; export REDWOOD_CACHE_URL='redis://user:pass@host:6379/0' ; run python app.py
08:00 Speaker 3 (Aisha): hmm for creds we prefer using vault, is there an example?
08:10 Speaker 2 (Jonas): yes we have a vault integration example in the repo, basically pull secrets at process start and set env vars or use a credentials provider pattern
08:28 Speaker 2 (Jonas): typescript example uses process.env and a typed client; snapshot of code: client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-small', input: '...' })  streaming uses client.chat.stream
08:50 Speaker 4 (Tom): ok are rate limits per-key? we have multiple services hitting the api
08:55 Speaker 1 (Maria): rate limits and quotas are configurable per-key and you can set per-route quotas; Dedicated gives higher throughput and rate control
09:10 Speaker 2 (Jonas): switching to console demo  token management is under settings, you can create scoped tokens with allowed routes and expiry
09:30 Speaker 2 (Jonas): also the Console quickstart has a one-click sample app that wires tokens into a small react demo; good for PoC
09:48 Speaker 3 (Aisha): will that sample app expose tokens? we can't have front-end tokens for sensitive calls
09:55 Speaker 2 (Jonas): sample is server-side; for browser flows you must use a proxy service or short-lived tokens via your backend and SSO flow
10:18 Speaker 3 (Priya): security question: do you support SAML IdP provisioning for users to access console?
10:23 Speaker 1 (Maria): yes, SSO via SAML/SCIM supported for Private and Enterprise accounts; Hosted also supports SAML for workspace access
10:40 Speaker 5 (Unknown): sorry jump in, is there client-side caching for embeddings?
10:47 Speaker 2 (Jonas): yeah you can cache embeddings locally and invalidate on TTL, Redwood Optimize also suggests caching hot prompts and embedding results to reduce cost
11:05 Speaker 2 (Jonas): back to perf: if you want deterministic latency, Dedicated with pinned model and padding-aware kernels is the way, otherwise hosted with routing policies and fallbacks is flexible
11:30 Speaker 3 (Aisha): ok lets talk pilot scope  we'd like a 2-week pilot to test transaction-screening with 100req/s burst to 300req/s, and measure p95 and cost per 1k tokens
11:45 Speaker 1 (Maria): good we usually run a benchmark with a representative prompt set, can you provide sample prompts and traffic profile?
11:55 Speaker 3 (Aisha): yes will share
12:12 Speaker 2 (Jonas): for benchmarks we'll capture latency percentiles, token counts, cost projections by quant/profile, and model quality metrics on your eval set
12:35 Speaker 4 (Tom): any gotchas for lambda cold starts and kv cache?
12:42 Speaker 2 (Jonas): cold starts can be mitigated by warming and using an external redis for cache; persistent connections also help reduce latency
13:05 Speaker 3 (Priya): do you log PII in transcripts? we need to know what is retained
13:14 Speaker 1 (Maria): by default hosted retains logs for x days but for enterprise/private you can disable retention or route logs to your archive; we'll share retention options in the security docs
13:35 Speaker 2 (Jonas): quick note on SDK versions  semver is respected, major bumps for breaking changes but runtime compatibility is maintained for minor/patch updates
13:58 Speaker 3 (Aisha): what's the process for model rollouts? we sometimes want canary two variants
14:05 Speaker 1 (Maria): Console supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies; you can pin model versions per route
14:30 Speaker 2 (Jonas): now a short demo of Optimize suggestions: show batching panel, recommended batch sizes, and suggested quantization profiles based on your token distribution
14:55 Speaker 3 (Aisha): those recommendations are based on real traffic right? or synthetic?
15:02 Speaker 2 (Jonas): usually both  initial recommendations from model profiles and similar workloads, refined by live traffic during the pilot
15:25 Speaker 4 (Tom): competitive: how do you compare to OpenAI or Anthropic on cost?
15:30 Speaker 1 (Maria): we don't want to get into price war here but the value prop is predictable inference economics + choice of deployment modes; we can share a cost model spreadsheet
15:50 Speaker 3 (Aisha): ok please send pricing examples tailored to our 1k-10k monthly usage bands
16:05 Speaker 2 (Jonas): wrapping up  recap of action items and deliverables
16:12 Speaker 1 (Maria): recap: we'll send quickstart repo, security docs, and schedule the perf pilot; jonas will prepare benchmark checklist; aisha to send prompts
16:30 Speaker 3 (Aisha): thanks, next call after we review the quickstart and security docs, aim for 3/29 for pilot kickoff
